title: Diego's $6 Coffee Is a $1,560 Yearly Bill

scenes.say: Diego spends $6 on coffee every workday, and it adds up to about $1,560 a year.
Here's the math. $6, five days a week, 52 weeks.
That's about $130 a month, poured into paper cups.
He doesn't want to quit coffee. He just wants a better deal.

visual.text: Keep the coffee. Fix the price.

scenes.say: At home, a good cup costs him about 75 cents.
So he keeps two café days a week, and brews the other three.
New yearly cost: about $740 instead of $1,560.
That's around $820 back every year, and still his Friday latte.
What's your daily habit worth? Do the math, because $6 a day is $1,560 a year.

visual.text: What does your daily habit cost?

question: What does your daily habit cost you per year? Do the math in the comments.
description: Diego buys a $6 coffee every workday — about $1,560 a year and roughly $7,800 over five years. Keeping two café days and brewing at home for about $0.75 a cup the other three drops it to around $740 a year. Prices are rounded US estimates.
